packageRules.description: Playwright: never bump unattended, and never bump one half alone. `playwright` and `@playwright/test` are held at the same version on purpose — Playwright bundles its own Chromium, and a different Chromium rasterises text and antialiasing differently. Every baseline on the `preview/main` branch was captured with this one, so a bump invalidates the whole set at once and the next PR's visual diff reports fake changes on every fixture. Adopting a new Playwright means republishing baselines in the same change, which a bot cannot do — hence `automerge: false`, overriding the preset's auto-land for minor/patch. Grouped so the two versions can never desync; dashboard-gated so the upgrade is a decision rather than a Monday morning surprise.

@types/vscode declares the minimum VS Code version this extension supports, and it has to stay in step with `engines.vscode` in package.json — which Renovate does not update. Bumping the types alone silently lets code compile against APIs older editors do not have; bumping both drops users on older VS Code. Either way it is a support-policy decision, so it waits on the dashboard and never auto-lands.

@types/node describes the Node the extension host runs on, which is the one inside VS Code's Electron, not the Node CI uses for scripts. The floor is `engines.vscode` (^1.115.0): VS Code 1.115.0 ships Electron 39.8.5 (its `.npmrc` `target`), whose Node is v22.22.1 (Electron's DEPS `node_version`). Typings newer than that let code compile against Node APIs the oldest supported editor does not have, so updates stay on the 22 line. Move this ceiling in the same change that raises `engines.vscode` and `@types/vscode`, to that editor's Electron Node major. The 26.x currently in package.json predates this rule (#101 took it from 24 to 26); Renovate does not roll a dependency back (`rollbackPrs` is off), so it proposes nothing for it until it is brought back inside the ceiling by hand.

`engines.vscode` is a RANGE, not a version to pin. The preset's `rangeStrategy: pin` is right for dependencies and wrong here: VS Code reads this field as a semver range against the running editor, so a pinned `1.135.0` means `only 1.135.0` and every later editor refuses to load the extension — which is exactly what #11 did, and what surfaced the day stable moved to 1.138.0. Disabled rather than re-ranged, because which floor this extension supports is the same support-policy decision as `@types/vscode` above, made by a human in the same change.
three and @types/three must move together: the typings track the runtime's version line exactly, and a mismatch fails the webview build rather than degrading gracefully.

Track the extension compatibility pin and automerge its upgrades once CI is green. A bump that moves the daemon BOM also needs `composePreviewDaemon` and the vendored protocol fixtures resynchronised, which Renovate cannot derive; the `Sync daemon pin` workflow does both on the `renovate/compose-ai-tools` branch and pushes them as `github-actions[bot]`. That author is in `gitIgnoredAuthors` above, so Renovate still counts the branch as unmodified and keeps rebasing and automerging it, rather than marking it edited and leaving it for a human (a rebase drops the bot commit, and the workflow writes it again). The pin names the plugin, but it is looked up as `compose-ai-tools-bom`, which every plugin release publishes to Maven Central at the same version: Renovate's maven datasource skips Maven Central for any package ending in `.gradle.plugin` ("skipping Maven Central for suspected Gradle plugin"), so looking up the marker always returned no-result and the pin sat at 2.35.0 without a PR.
